policy: Correct and then fail-closed on generated-fallback balcony slab/railing interfaces before realtime reflection or native-4K evidence. This is source/scene construction QA only and awards zero Visual Fidelity points without actual rendered evidence.
manufactureModel: The benchmark railing is treated as a circa-2000 manufactured aluminum/metal balcony handrail assembly rather than geometry emerging directly from the concrete slab.

Vertical posts are mechanically anchored at the balcony slab edge through discrete base plates/anchor fasteners; the post can extend into/through the attachment zone, but the visible base plate must sit on the slab top rather than be buried inside the slab.
The slab fascia is reinforced-concrete/cementitious construction and therefore must inherit the balcony-floor concrete material response, not the anodized-aluminum rail material.
The lower horizontal rail is a fabricated rail member above the slab top; it must not be hidden below the walking-surface plane.
The low divider bracket is mechanically grounded at the slab top so its contact shadow and fastener relationship have a physical cause.
installationSequence: Resolve each bay's actual balcony-floor top plane from the persisted renderer bounds and verify it remains within the locked generated-fallback floor-top tolerance.

Place the concrete fascia directly below that top plane so its upper face is flush with the walking-surface elevation and its extra thickness projects downward rather than upward into the railing zone.
Seat each galvanized base plate on the slab top with zero intentional air gap.
Seat each visible anchor-bolt head into the base-plate top by the small controlled embed target so it reads as tightened hardware rather than a floating cylinder.
Keep the lower rail bottom roughly 70 mm above the slab top so it is visibly separate from the slab and mechanically intersects the vertical post line.
Seat the low divider bracket on the slab top; preserve the existing higher bracket and fasteners as separate manufactured hardware.
interfacesGapsSeals: fascia top to balcony-floor top: flush within contactTolerance
base-plate bottom to slab top: flush within contactTolerance
anchor-bolt head to base-plate top: controlled 1-6 mm visual embed, target 3 mm
lower-rail bottom to slab top: 50-100 mm allowed, target 70 mm
low divider-bracket bottom to slab top: flush within contactTolerance
base plate must laterally contain the corresponding existing vertical rail-post centerline

materialsFinish.fascia: same concrete/cementitious PBR material as BalconyFloor_<floor>_<bay>; dielectric mineral surface, no metallic response
materialsFinish.basePlateAndBolts: aged dark galvanized steel hardware; metallic response only where physically exposed
materialsFinish.weatheringRule: rain/UV/runoff changes roughness/albedo only where exposure/source metadata provides a cause; no arbitrary rust or baked highlight

orientationExposureAging: fascia front edge receives sun/rain and can show ledge-driven runoff below the top edge
base plates and anchor heads are rain/sun exposed and may carry localized oxidation/runoff at fastener sources
horizontal rail upward faces collect water/dust more than vertical faces
contact/grime must accumulate at interfaces and recesses rather than as uniform random noise
geometryVsMaterialDetail: slab/fascia thickness, base plate, bolt head, bracket, rail clearance and post relationship are geometry
oxide dulling, micro-scratches, chalking, concrete aggregate-scale normal response and water spotting are material/microdetail
contact shadows and grazing highlights must arise from real geometry + coherent lighting, never painted into albedo

lookdevBrief.frontal: Native 3840x2160 facade crop: verify fascia reads as concrete, all seven post base plates sit on the slab top, and no plate/lower rail disappears into the slab.
lookdevBrief.oblique: 35-45 degree oblique balcony-services crop: reveal slab thickness, plate thickness, bolt heads, lower-rail clearance and bracket contact with coherent contact shadow.
lookdevBrief.grazing: Midsummer grazing-light crop: concrete fascia must retain broad dielectric response while aluminum/galvanized hardware separates by angular highlight width/Fresnel; reject painted edge highlights.
lookdevBrief.macro100Percent: Inspect plate/slab and bolt/plate interfaces at 100% pixels for floating gaps, z-fighting, buried hardware, light leaks or impossible intersection.
